items.titleEn: Kioxia stock falls after issuing soft guidance: will it crash to ¥10k?
items.summaryEn: Sell Kioxia. Soft guidance plus “timing” excuses still leaves operating profit below consensus, and the stock is already in a technical breakdown (near ¥10,000 target, death-cross risk). If AI funding tightens, memory demand expectations get marked down again, keeping pressure on valuation. Key Risk: AI capex doesn’t slow and Kioxia’s March-quarter growth re-accelerates fast enough to force analysts to raise estimates. Sell MEM. The article shows broad memory weakness (Micron/Samsung/SK Hynix down, ETF down >20%), meaning the risk is sector-wide, not just Kioxia. If investors fear funding stress for data centers, the whole memory complex reprices lower together.

items.titleEn: SoftBank stock at risk of hitting ¥3k as OpenAI woes mount, Arm earnings loom
items.summaryEn: Sell SoftBank. The thesis is a double hit: OpenAI fundraising missed its target ($11B vs $30B) and at a lower valuation than planned, signaling AI capital is tightening; plus SoftBank’s core holdings (Arm and Intel) are in a broad risk-off slide. Chart risk is explicit: a potential death cross and support at ¥4,334; if it breaks, downside targets ¥3,000. Key Risk: OpenAI secures a much larger, faster follow-on round (or SoftBank’s AI-linked assets re-rate), stopping the valuation compression and triggering a rebound above ¥4,334. Sell Arm. SoftBank is the dominant holder (86.4%), so Arm weakness directly drags SoftBank. Arm is also facing a looming earnings spotlight; with the stock already down ~54% YTD, any guidance that confirms demand softness or delays in AI/compute adoption will likely extend the selloff.

items.titleEn: News Corp stock analysis as judge tosses Trump's WSJ lawsuit ahead of earnings
items.summaryEn: Buy News Corp (NWSA). The judge tossed Trump’s $10B WSJ lawsuit on First Amendment grounds, removing a headline overhang right before earnings. Even if the market reaction is mild, the next catalyst is fundamentals: recent revenue growth (digital real estate, publishing, Dow Jones) and strong free cash flow ($811M). Technicals are stretched (below 50-day, under 23.6% fib, double-top), so a clean legal headline + earnings can trigger a sharp mean-reversion bounce toward the 50-day. Key Risk: Earnings disappoint (revenue or EPS guidance) and the stock breaks below $27.9 support, turning the bounce into a continued downtrend. Buy Dow Jones-linked exposure inside News Corp: NWSA over the broader media basket. The lawsuit dismissal reduces perceived legal/regulatory tail risk for WSJ/Dow Jones assets, which should support a higher valuation multiple if earnings show steady ad/subscription and real-estate momentum. Pair with selling weaker, more legally exposed media names only if they trade on similar headline risk—otherwise stay long NWSA as the cleaner beneficiary.

items.titleEn: Big Tech's AI bill meets a 'Big Cash Burn' issue: are investors' fears justified?
items.summaryEn: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler in the article showing AI spend translating into both growth and cash: Azure up 48% and free cash flow of $18.6B (about $10B above expectations). The market is punishing “cash burn,” so MSFT should rerate as the cleanest proof that AI capex can still produce shareholder cash. Key Risk: Azure growth slows sharply and free cash flow turns down, proving AI spend isn’t converting into durable returns. Alphabet has strong Cloud demand (Google Cloud revenue $30.71B, more than doubled) but the cash reality is ugly: free cash flow -$9.07B and slowing Search/YouTube ad growth. With investors already worried about Nasdaq 100 cash burn, GOOGL’s negative FCF plus legacy revenue pressure makes it the higher-risk “AI story” versus peers.

items.titleEn: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week. "We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, a lawyer representing one of the young women suing both companies, said in a statement.
